description:
Observation from the fz-kdt.101 build (2026-08-31): jobs/transport.rs:141 (direct_surfaces) and :2094 (rendered) sort by ShapeId::as_u32 -- shape-interner mint order, the same hazard class fz-kdt.101 fixed for Ty ids but on a different interner. NO MEASURED LEAK: 00420/00183/range_map are byte-identical FIFO vs LIFO with these untouched, so either the sorted sets are singletons in practice or shapes intern in schedule-stable order on these drives. Fixing it needs a canonical ShapeId comparator (recursive over ShapeDescr, the order.rs cmp_ty pattern on the shape arena) which does not exist. Sequence: only worth building if a leak is ever demonstrated (LIFO-style perturbation moving canon through these two sorts) or if a shape-heavy fixture lands; until then this is a recorded hazard, not work.

WIDENED (fz-kdt.101 refuter, 2026-08-31) -- three more corners of the
same recorded-hazard class, all unproven leaks, all in packaging:
1. Wrapper tie fallback crosses functions on MINT ORDER: the wrapper
   canon key (callable|arity|return_form|boundaries) excludes the OWNER,
   so two byte-identical wrappers owned by DIFFERENT functions would tie
   and fall to FunctionId mint order (agenda-ordered reference/definition
   jobs, world.rs:870-884/2802-2814 -- not strictly parse order). All
   measured twins are same-function siblings; the executables half is
   structurally safe (canon keys embed function labels).
2. jobs/backend.rs:1319 callable_boundaries sorted by CallableId::as_u32.
3. jobs/backend.rs:1324 boundary_ids sorted by BoundaryId::as_u32.
Fix shape if a leak is ever demonstrated: canonical comparators for the
respective interners (the order.rs pattern), or include the owner label
in the wrapper canon key.
title: ShapeId mint-order sorts in transport packaging: same hazard shape as fz-kdt.101, unproven leak, no canonical comparator exists
